newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale des Eaux to unveil telecoms partnership.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux to unveil telecoms partnership.

text.p: Generale des Eaux, the large French utilities group, said on Wednesday it would unveil the names of the international partners for its new Cegetel telecommunications unit on Thursday.
The company said in a statement its executive chairman Jean-Marie Messier would hold a news conference at 0900 GMT, surrounded by representatives of the new partners.
But a spokesman added that because companies involved were quoted groups a statement was likely before the opening of the stock market.
The spokesman declined to comment on the identities.
Among most likely candidates are AT&T, Vodafone Plc, Southwestern Belland Germany's Veba or Mannesmann. British Telecoms Plc and MCI Communciations Corp could also feature.
A BT spokeswoman contacted in London said: "We do not respond to rumours and speculation."

Messier announced the creation of Cegetel at the start of the month. The unit will group all the company's telecommunications activities and aims to become France's number two operator after France Telecom.

Generale des Eaux is already the most active rival to France Telecom. It controls the Societe Francaise de Radiotelephonie (SFR), the country's second-biggest mobile telecoms operator. Vodafone and Southwestern Bell are also stakeholders in SFR.

It also has the Siris joint-venture with Unisource for telecommunications services to businesses. Unisource NV is a grouping of Dutch Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, Sweden's Telia, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica.
Unisource and AT&T are working together in a transatlantic alliance rivalling the links between France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp, as well as one between British Telecom and MCI.
There have been rumours that Generale des Eaux could link up with British Telecom/MCI instead of AT&T.
Generale des Eaux plans to invest four billion francs ($784.1 million) in telecommunications between 1997 and 1999 of which 2.3 billion in mobile telecommunications.
It valued the telecoms market in France in 1995 at 117 billion francs, of which six billion is for mobiles, and expects this to grow to 187 billion in 2003, with 55 billion for mobiles.

Messier himself will chair Cegetel and the group will hold "strong majority control." But due to the huge investment needed to set up infrastructure and cover launch costs, strategic partners are needed.
Cegetel was set up ahead of full liberalisation of the French, and other European, telecoms sector which will see the loss of France Telecom's remaining monopoly positions in the amrket.
France Telecom is slated to be partially privatised in the spring of 1997. ($1=5.101 French Franc)
